description: The hardened core of an old AXIOM long-range navigation beacon. Its stored timing and link records can extend the restored KX-91 operational picture.
A sealed telemetry archive from a lost AXIOM support node. It contains enough historical fault data to improve KX-91 field diagnostics.
A hardened logistics manifest from an abandoned AXIOM-linked cache. Mara can use it to reconcile several lost maintenance lots.
Recover the core of a distant AXIOM-compatible beacon so KX-91 can rebuild part of its long-range navigation picture.

effect.u_message: The recovered beacon history is merged into KX-91's long-range navigation set. The aircraft now has a much cleaner picture beyond the local AXIOM sector.

dialogue.describe: Recover a distant navigation beacon core for the restored KX-91.
dialogue.offer: Owning the aircraft is not the same thing as having a network to support it. One old beacon still answers intermittently. It is far enough away that this is exactly the sort of run KX-91 was built for. Bring back its hardened core.
dialogue.accepted: I marked the site. The core is the only part I care about; leave the mast where it fell.
dialogue.rejected: Then we keep flying with a very local picture of a very large world.
dialogue.advice: The target is an old radio site. The hardened core should be near the control electronics.
dialogue.inquire: Did you recover the beacon core?
dialogue.success: Good. This gives us timing history, old link geometry, and something the KX flight computer can actually correlate against.
dialogue.success_lie: That is not the beacon core.
dialogue.failure: Then the outer navigation picture stays incomplete.

description: Destroy a hostile autonomous unit on a distant corridor used by AXIOM field routes.

dialogue.describe: Clear a rogue autonomous sentry from a long-range AXIOM corridor.
dialogue.offer: One of our old corridor sentries came back on the net with a broken authority table. It is treating every contact as unknown-hostile. I want it gone before we start using that route again. This is a field operation, not a salvage job.
dialogue.accepted: Target marked. Do not try to recover it intact; the authority core is exactly what I do not trust.
dialogue.rejected: Then the corridor stays red on my board.
dialogue.advice: Open ground favors the sentry. Use terrain, smoke, or range discipline. KX-91 gets you there; it does not make you immortal.
dialogue.success: Confirmed. The corridor is no longer being watched by a machine with a corrupted friend list.

description: Recover a sealed AXIOM flight-telemetry archive from a remote electrical support node.

effect.u_message: Viktor folds the recovered fault history into the KX diagnostic model. Several intermittent field failures become predictable instead of mysterious.

dialogue.describe: Recover historical KX-support telemetry from a remote power node.
dialogue.offer: The aircraft works. I would like it to keep working. One support node logged years of flight-system faults before the network died. Its telemetry archive would let me turn several unknown failure modes into scheduled maintenance instead of emergencies.
dialogue.accepted: Substation marked. The archive is sealed; bring the module, not a printout.
dialogue.rejected: Then we continue learning failures one expensive surprise at a time.
dialogue.advice: The archive should be inside the service area, not on the high-voltage side.
dialogue.inquire: Do you have the telemetry archive?
dialogue.success: Excellent. Historical faults are ugly, but they are measurable. Measurable is repairable.
dialogue.success_lie: No. This is not the support archive.
dialogue.failure: Then our maintenance model stays shallower than I would like.

description: Recover a distant AXIOM logistics manifest and close the first post-restoration field-operations cycle.

effect.u_message: Mara reconciles the manifest against AXIOM's surviving inventory. The first post-restoration KX-91 operations cycle is closed, and she establishes a recurring flight-support maintenance allocation for you.

dialogue.describe: Recover a lost logistics manifest from a distant warehouse.
dialogue.offer: All this flying is useful, but useful machines eat parts. I found a warehouse entry tied to three maintenance lots that never made it back onto our books. I do not need you to haul the warehouse home. Bring me the hardened manifest so I can reconstruct what is still worth chasing.
dialogue.accepted: Warehouse marked. Find the manifest and come home. If the shelves are empty, I still want the record.
dialogue.rejected: Fine. Then I keep budgeting flight support from guesses.
dialogue.advice: The manifest is a hardened tablet-sized record, not ordinary paperwork.
dialogue.inquire: Did the warehouse still have the AXIOM manifest?
dialogue.success: Yes. This closes enough gaps that I can stop treating every KX sortie as a one-off emergency. I will keep a flight-support lot available for you once per week.
dialogue.success_lie: That is not the logistics manifest.
dialogue.failure: Then the maintenance allocation stays provisional.

effect.u_message: Mara signs out the weekly KX-91 flight-support lot: one full dense cell, one nanomaterial pack, and one EMP grenade.

false_effect.u_message: The next KX-91 flight-support lot is not due yet.
